clue.text: Book adapted for millionth serial

indicators.note: something adapted is reworked into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A novel turned into a serial that runs to a millionth episode.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adapted' rearranges MILLIONTHSERIAL; 'for' is only a link. The Silmarillion is Tolkien's posthumously published book of Middle-earth legends.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolkien's collection of legends is a published volume, so it is an example of a book.

clue.text: One of the three said to be in it?

definitions.text: One of the three said to be in it?

parts.words: One of the three said to be in it?
parts.note: the word under discussion is said in three spoken beats, and the clue asks for the name of one such beat of speech

explanation.surface: A riddle about one of three things supposedly inside something.
explanation.walkthrough: The trick is self-reference: the word that answers has three spoken units, and the clue's 'it' is that very word, so one of its three units is what is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of pronunciation is one of three spoken parts in a three-part word, the riddle's description.

clue.text: Statement of belief's inadequate language

indicators.note: inadequate means falling short, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a creed is a formal statement of religious belief

explanation.surface: A complaint that a declaration of faith is poorly expressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inadequate' cuts the last letter from CREED. Cree is a language of the Algonquian family spoken by First Nations people in Canada.
explanation.definitionFit: Cree is the tongue of a North American indigenous people, so it is an example of a language.

clue.text: In a way satire could be funny, we admitted

indicators.note: admitted means let in, so one piece is placed inside the other
funny here means odd or altered, so the word satire could be scrambled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Satire might well be comic, we concede, in some fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be funny' signals the anagram of satire and 'admitted' the insertion; 'In a way' looks like part of the surface but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom meaning so to speak or in a manner of speaking, the same hedge as 'in a way'.

clue.text: Picture of one crossing the Red Sea?

definitions.meaning: a picture made from small pieces of coloured stone or glass set in cement

definitions.text: of one crossing the Red Sea?
definitions.meaning: an adjective meaning relating to Moses, who led the Israelites across the Red Sea

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is the adjective from Moses, as in the Mosaic law; the question mark flags the playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a tiled picture and anything belonging to Moses, the leader who crossed the Red Sea.

clue.text: Urges a boy to produce food

parts.note: to egg someone on is to urge them, so urges gives eggs
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: Someone presses a young lad to cook a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A salad of chopped boiled eggs and mayonnaise is a dish, so it is an example of food.

clue.text: Soon Pasquale's turning up as Pasquale?

parts.note: anon is an old word for soon

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up reads the piece from bottom to top, so it is backwards

parts.note: the setter is Pasquale, so Pasquale's means my

explanation.surface: The setter wonders whether he will soon appear under his own name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reverses MY to YM. The setter's possessive gives MY, a common crossword convention; the definition is Pasquale itself, a pen-name.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasquale is a pseudonym, and an assumed or concealed name is called an anonym.

clue.text: Former President could be sadly disgraced — a sting found out

indicators.note: sadly here means badly or in a sorry state, so the following letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A former head of state might be disgraced when a sting operation exposes him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be sadly' rearranges DISGRACEDASTING. Valéry Giscard d'Estaing was President of France from 1974 to 1981.
explanation.definitionFit: Valéry Giscard d'Estaing led France in the 1970s, so he is an example of a past head of state.

clue.text: What about that report of fodder reaching city shortly!

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: hay is dried grass used as fodder

indicators.note: shortly means cut short, so the last letter goes

parts.note: Preston is a city in Lancashire, England

explanation.surface: An exclamation at news of hay arriving in a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'report of' turns HAY into HEY; 'shortly' cuts PRESTON to PRESTO. Preston is a city in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: The conjuror's exclamation announces a surprise, much like saying 'what about that!'

clue.text: Spirits of the first verse in the book

parts.note: Gen is the abbreviation for Genesis, the first book of the Bible
the first verse of the first chapter is cited I.I, chapter 1 verse 1

explanation.surface: Ghosts appearing in the opening lines of scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: A Bible reference is book, chapter, verse: Genesis 1:1 is written Gen I.I.
explanation.definitionFit: Genii is a plural of genie or genius in its sense of a guardian spirit, so the word means spirits.

clue.text: In the street one like ET is conspicuous

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street
ET, the film extraterrestrial, is an alien

explanation.surface: An extraterrestrial standing in the road would certainly stand out.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening 'In' is the container signal, not a link. ET is the alien of Spielberg's 1982 film.
explanation.definitionFit: Salient means prominent or most noticeable, a synonym of conspicuous.

clue.text: Element wanting change to back pair in soccer team

indicators.text: wanting change to back pair in
indicators.note: wanting a change at the back means the last two letters of the team's name are replaced

parts.note: Arsenal is a London football club

explanation.surface: A football club needs to change its pair of defenders.
explanation.walkthrough: Arsenal is a London soccer club; replacing its last two letters, AL, with IC gives the element. The clue does not say where IC comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: Arsenic is a chemical element, atomic number 33, the poison of murder mysteries.

clue.text: Reverse of old coin shows timber wolf

indicators.note: reverse of reads the coin's name backwards, playing on a coin's reverse face

parts.note: an obol was a small coin of ancient Greece

explanation.surface: The back of an ancient coin depicts a wolf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reverse of' reads OBOL backwards; on a coin the reverse is the tails side, which makes the surface plausible.
explanation.definitionFit: Lobo is a North American name for the grey or timber wolf, from Spanish.

clue.text: Form of English you may get from Mabel, a char

indicators.note: the letters are something you may get by reshuffling the given words

explanation.surface: A cleaning lady named Mabel speaks her own kind of English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'you may get from' rearranges MABELACHAR. Beach-la-mar is an English-based pidgin of the western Pacific, also called Bislama.
explanation.definitionFit: This Pacific pidgin is built on English vocabulary, so it is a variety of the language.

clue.text: Chemical requirement in a fab colour

parts.note: fab and ace are both slang for excellent
a tone is a shade of colour

explanation.surface: A lab needs a substance with a splendid hue.
explanation.definitionFit: Acetone is a solvent that a lab or nail salon needs, so it is a chemical required for work.

clue.text: Label detailing performers is officially noted

definitions.meaning: a playful reading: the sleeve or label of a disc lists who is playing on it

explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is cryptic: performers named on a disc's label are literally there on the disc.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for formally registered, and also literally means appearing on a disc.

clue.text: Nothing by novice would ultimately help someone experienced

parts.note: O, the figure zero, is nothing
L is a learner, from the L-plate on a learner driver's car

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the next word

parts.note: a hand is help, as in lend a hand

explanation.surface: A beginner with nothing would be grateful for a veteran's assistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' takes D, the end of 'would'. L for learner comes from British L-plates on new drivers' cars.
explanation.definitionFit: An old hand is a veteran of some activity, so the phrase means a person with long experience.

clue.text: Take care of a public exterior — get paint

definitions.text: Take care of a public exterior — get paint

parts.words: Take care of a public exterior — get paint
parts.note: read one way, it is the garment that protects you when out in public; read another, the final layer of paint laid on top

explanation.surface: Advice on looking after a building's façade: buy some paint.
explanation.walkthrough: Both readings point to the same compound: a heavy coat worn outdoors, and a top layer of paint.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a warm outer garment worn outdoors and also a final protective layer of paint.

clue.text: A nameless fantasiser being spicy

indicators.note: nameless says the letter N, short for name, is removed

parts.note: a romantic is a dreamer who fantasises

explanation.surface: A dreamer with no name has a fiery temperament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nameless' works as two parts: N is the standard abbreviation for name, and 'less' removes it from the dreamer.
explanation.definitionFit: Aromatic means having a strong pleasant smell, as spices do, so it is close to spicy.

clue.text: Vessel that may help liven up a formal party

definitions.meaning: a ship built to cut through frozen seas

definitions.text: that may help liven up a formal party
definitions.meaning: a game or remark that dispels stiffness among strangers

explanation.walkthrough: One sense is a ship, the other a social device for breaking awkward silence.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a ship that clears frozen water and a device for easing social tension.

clue.text: Exuberant Henry descending to become smutty

indicators.note: in a down clue descending moves the letter further down the column

parts.note: hearty means vigorous and exuberant
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A cheerful Henry slides into vulgar jokes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'descending' moves H from the top of HEARTY lower down, giving EARTHY.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthy humour is coarse and frank about bodily matters, close to smutty.

clue.text: Remove tar stuck to behind

parts.note: a tar is a sailor, as is an AB, an able seaman
late means behind time

explanation.surface: Instructions for getting tar off one's backside.
explanation.walkthrough: Tar and AB both mean sailor; 'stuck to' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To ablate is to take material away by erosion, melting or surgery, so it means remove.

clue.text: Do they provide endless encouragement? Yes and no!

definitions.text: Do they provide endless encouragement? Yes and no!

indicators.note: endless drops the final letter

parts.note: a boost is a lift in morale, encouragement

explanation.surface: A question whether jeers count as support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts BOOST to BOOS. Yes: they are encouragement without its end; no: jeers are hardly supportive.
explanation.definitionFit: Jeers from a crowd are the opposite of support, which the 'no' of the clue admits.

clue.text: Enthusiastic jazz singer behind London theatre

indicators.note: behind puts the singer after the theatre

parts.note: the Lyric is a theatre on Shaftesbury Avenue in London's West End
Al Jolson starred in The Jazz Singer, the first talking picture

explanation.surface: A keen jazz vocalist stands at the back of a West End theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: AL comes from Al Jolson, star of the 1927 film The Jazz Singer; the Lyric is a West End theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: To wax lyrical is to speak with great enthusiasm, so lyrical can mean enthusiastic.

clue.text: Pet beginning to ail when idiot's stuffed in ice cream

indicators.note: stuffed in means pushed inside another word

parts.note: a cat is a household pet
an ass is an idiot

indicators.note: beginning to points to the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A pet starts to sicken after a fool overfeeds it ice cream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stuffed in' is the container signal and 'beginning to' takes the first letter of 'ail'. Cassata is a Sicilian dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: Cassata is an Italian ice cream dessert with candied fruit, so it is an example of ice cream.

clue.text: For the most part be frugal with cream

indicators.note: for the most part keeps all but the last letter

parts.note: to skimp is to be sparing or frugal

explanation.surface: Advice to go easy on the cream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For the most part' drops the last letter of SKIMP. 'Cream' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To cream milk is to take off its top layer, which is to skim it.

clue.text: More's trouble — head being chopped off

indicators.note: a beheading removes the first letter, apt for Sir Thomas More

parts.note: bother is trouble

explanation.surface: Sir Thomas More's troubles ended with the axe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head being chopped off' removes B from BOTHER. The surface recalls Thomas More, beheaded by Henry VIII; 'More' here just means additional.
explanation.definitionFit: Other can mean additional or further, as in 'one other thing', so it equals more.

clue.text: Reverse of skill shown by publication — not English usage

indicators.note: reverse of reads the word backwards

parts.note: art is skill

indicators.note: E is the abbreviation for English, removed here

parts.note: an edition is a published issue

explanation.surface: A comment that the opposite of skill appears in a publication that avoids English usage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reverse of' turns ART into TRA; 'not English' removes E from EDITION to give DITION.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradition is an established custom, which is one meaning of usage.
